data.narrative:
Deep Atomic is a pre-seed nuclear energy company founded by William G.J. Theron. The valuation universe comprises 10 comparable companies: 3 public entities (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 7 private firms including Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy. The broader nuclear energy sector contains 6 identifiable peers.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this analysis. The dataset contains insufficient narrow-stage comparables—zero same-stage pre-seed transactions, one adjacent-stage datapoint, and zero similar-tier valuations meet the three-datapoint minimum threshold required for statistical reliability. Expanding to all-sector medians would introduce unacceptable selection bias given the heterogeneity in capital requirements, technical risk, and commercialization timelines across the nuclear energy landscape. The available comp set, while broad, does not support triangulation via conventional multiples-based approaches at this early stage.

Without sufficient quantitative anchors from the peer set, this valuation cannot be supported by standard VC methodologies. A credible range would require either (1) expansion of pre-seed nuclear energy transaction data, (2) application of first-principles cost-of-capital modeling tied to technical milestones, or (3) scenario-weighted probability of success frameworks tied to regulatory and technical execution risk. The primary uncertainty is the absence of comparable pre-seed nuclear transactions, which limits the ability to calibrate founder equity stakes and capital efficiency expectations against market precedent.
